endorsements.quote: design confidence thresholds that trigger human review of critical LaJ judgments when concordance across evaluators is low.

unlisted_practices: Provide evidence for the rationale behind metric weighting in LLM-as-Judge evaluations and argue that high or low scores in one metric will not undermine overall safety of the judgement.
Delegate metric calculations in LLM-as-Judge evaluations to external deterministic tools or traceable program code rather than relying on LLM next-token prediction.
Define explicit quantified criteria for soft evaluation metrics such as correctness and specificity used by LLM-as-Judge evaluators.
Test that LLM evaluators recognise all synonym and abbreviation variants across the full range of possible inputs.
Question the value of soft LLM-judged metrics in safety-critical evaluations even when they are reliably consistent.
Define domain-specific critical quality gates with clinical specialists that cap evaluation scores when critical risks are missed.
Ensure assurance arguments show that omission in LLM outputs can be detected or will not contribute to known hazards.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual/framework paper proposing evaluation metrics, confidence thresholds, and human review strategies for LLM safety (including in clinical workflows such as triage) rather than an empirical study.
